methods.label: Make the counts equal
methods.explanation:
With one additional nickel, Leah would have \(14\) coins, split equally between pennies and nickels. She would therefore have \(14\div2=7\) of each.

Removing that hypothetical nickel leaves \(7\) pennies and \(6\) nickels. A penny is worth \(1\) cent and a nickel is worth \(5\) cents, so her original coins are worth
\[
7\cdot1+6\cdot5=7+30=\boxed{37}\text{ cents},
\]
choice C.
